question: In a patient with tetanus, human tetanus immunoglobulin (HTIG) can effectively neutralise tetanospasmin that has already bound to peripheral nerve terminals.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. HTIG (or equine antitetanus serum) neutralises only unbound, circulating tetanospasmin. Once toxin has bound to peripheral nerve terminals and ascended to the spinal cord, it cannot be removed — hence the clinical course depends on pre-bound toxin, and recovery requires new synaptic sprouting (weeks to months).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct that this is false. HTIG neutralises free circulating tetanospasmin only — it cannot reverse binding once the toxin has entered the nervous system. This is why early wound debridement and HTIG administration are critical to prevent more toxin from entering circulation.
